newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Late import covering pushes down Sri Lanka rupee.
newsitem.headline: Late import covering pushes down Sri Lanka rupee.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee, which gained in early trade on high call rates, closed softer due to late import covering demand for dollars, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 56.64 after rising to 56.53, they said.
"High call money rates pushed down the dollar but late import covering demand saw the currency gain some lost ground," said a Sampath Bank dealer.
Call money closed at 29 percent, after moving between 26 and 32 percent, dealers said.

The Central Bank's removal of more than one billion rupees from the system at last week's Treasury Bill auction, and increased cash withdrawals from banks, had put pressure on money rates, dealers said.
"Traditionally, cash withdrawals from banks start rising in late November, as corporates start paying festival advances, bonuses, etc," said one.
It is only in the middle of January that this money finds its way back into the system, he said.
